correctness.rationale: Every admissible cyclic host is exactly a closed directed walk on the no-11 overlap graph. A finite directed-state BFS with bit masks exhausts all possible reversal-class coverage walks for orders two through six; direct exhaustive enumeration of every legal circular host below the candidate optimum independently excludes shorter solutions. Five explicit circular witnesses achieve the bounds. There is no extrapolation beyond order six.

originality.rationale: The 2016 primary unoriented-de-Bruijn paper treats unconstrained words and general Eulerizations, not the exact golden-mean finite threshold. The indexed oriented golden-mean cyclic covering theorem determines lengths 3,6,10,17,28 for orders two through six, and an indexed small-order census enumerates optimal oriented cycles, but neither implies the reversal-relaxed order-six minimum 23. Unrestricted binary reversal covers concern a different source set. This full finite reversal boundary was not identified in searches; unindexed prior small calculations remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The first order where ignoring orientation strictly reduces a universal constrained cyclic covering length is a natural structural boundary, not an arbitrary slice. Exact savings of five symbols (23 versus 28, over 17 percent) at the first positive case measure the intrinsic cost of orientation in no-11 synchronization word families. Complete finite exclusion and explicit witnesses are provided, not just a computed upper bound.
